references.text: The parallel commandment in Deuteronomy that restates the Ten Commandments. Here the verb חמד (covet) is used in the same way as in Exodus 20:17.
Achan admits that he coveted (חמד) spoils from Jericho, illustrating the consequence of breaking the command against coveting.
Proverbs warns against coveting (חמד) another man's wife, directly linking to the prohibition in this commandment.
Micah condemns those who covet (חמד) fields and houses and seize them by force, an example of violating this commandment.
Paul quotes the command against coveting (ἐπιθυμέω) and explains how the law revealed sin in his heart.
Paul lists the command against coveting as part of the law's summary in the command to love.
Paul warns against greed (πλεονεξία), which is closely tied to coveting and idolatry.
Greed (πλεονεξία) is identified as idolatry, linking coveting to spiritual adultery.
The exhortation to live free from love of money reflects the principle of not coveting what belongs to others.
James describes how coveting (ἐπιθυμέω) leads to conflict and sin, in line with the commandment's warning.
Highlights the connection between inner sin (coveting) and outward action (breaking the marriage covenant).
Highlights the connection between inner sin (coveting) and its economic consequences.
